Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

| Runner | Model | What it does |

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

A cancelled required check is never a verdict: the sweep skips cancelled conclusions by design and fail-validation owns red, so this rule cannot fight them — it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, it only re-runs GitHub Actions runs. GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). CANCELLED is read with branch-protection semantics: the LATEST check run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp does NOT act (#695 review fix). NOT failure — failure paths exist; NOT pending-with-active-runs — the localAction probes every run on the head (hasActiveDispatchedRun pattern widened to all events) and skips while anything is in flight. localAction rerun_cancelled_checks re-runs (gh run rerun) the latest attempt-1 cancelled run per required context and posts a once-per-head marker comment citing the evidence — ONLY when the rerun set covers every cancelled context (a partial set defers the marker so the uncovered contexts stay actionable; #695). relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |

— first healthy provider wins.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |

— first healthy provider wins.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |

| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |

relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

CANCELLED is read with branch-protection semantics: the LATEST check run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp does NOT act (#695 review fix). NOT failure — failure paths exist; NOT pending-with-active-runs — the localAction probes every run on the head (hasActiveDispatchedRun pattern widened to all events) and skips while anything is in flight. localAction rerun_cancelled_checks re-runs (gh run rerun) the latest attempt-1 cancelled run per required context and posts a once-per-head marker comment citing the evidence — ONLY when the rerun set covers every cancelled context (a partial set defers the marker so the uncovered contexts stay actionable; #695). Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |

— first healthy provider wins.

# gh-857 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: GitHub-minted "required-check placeholder" check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no
numeric run id, `app=github-actions`) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` forever on heads whose real
verdict is green — SM verdict stamps (later, completed/success) never override them (live fa #1457,
9 instances) — so the oldest-approved FIFO burns the serial mutex in arm→dispatch→green→pinned→
sweep→re-arm cycles (~35 min/hour).

**Root cause**: Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head). A placeholder is
pending and link-less; nobody concludes it. The SM's remedy today (`js/smAgent.js` gh-852
PLACEHOLDER GATE, `validate_pr`) only knows the expensive cure — a fresh-sha silent update + full
CI re-dispatch — and never tries to conclude the placeholder in place, even though the head carries
a concluded-success dispatched run (the real green verdict) and no live run is producing the
pinned context.

**Impact**: Any placeholder-pinned green PR is unmergeable without operator action; the per-PR
reset cap (gh-852 AC2) eventually parks it entirely.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket goal + ACs):
- In the gh-852 placeholder gate (`validate_pr`), BEFORE the cap/pool/reset steps: when the head
  has a real green verdict (`greenCoverRun` — newest completed-success dispatched run; AC3: red
  never concludes green, verdict mirror only) and the whole-head run rollup shows NO active run
  (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` + `hasActiveHeadRun`; AC2: a placeholder with a live run behind it is
  never concluded), PATCH each placeholder check-run via Checks API to
  `status=completed, conclusion=success` with output referencing the covering run — using the
  workflow token (`jobParams.silentToken`) swap, same pattern as the gh-848 belt
  (`concludeOrphanedCheckRuns`). The check-run `id` is now carried by
  `checkRunZombies.placeholders()` (pure-module additive change).
- When every placeholder concludes: no fresh-sha reset, no CI dispatch — the head unblocks the
  same tick (the PATCH fires a check-run-completed event → the event-driven mergeBot fast path /
  the next merge-validated tick consumes the green CLEAN head). AC1.
- When the PATCH is rejected (403 ownership — the Actions app's check-runs refuse the workflow
  token): post the 403 evidence to the PR (the gh-848 trail) and fall through to the existing
  gh-852 fresh-sha reset unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: none in-repo (gh-852/#853 implemented the fresh-sha reset this change
supersedes as the first-choice cure; it remains as the fallback).

relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,
   for fleets where different repos run different bots:
   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
   nor re-arms `agent:rework` (external semantics — the verdict comment
   is the whole report).

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the review runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE='[{"provider":"kimi",...},{"provider":"zai","model":"glm-5.3"}]'`
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting

So the machine factory rules ("merge-validated": green + CLEAN → squash-merge) are project config — in the consuming repo's `.dmtools/config.js` smRules. **Bug**: GitHub-minted "required-check placeholder" check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no

sweep→re-arm cycles (~35 min/hour).

**Root cause**: Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head). A placeholder is
pending and link-less; nobody concludes it. The SM's remedy today (`js/smAgent.js` gh-852
PLACEHOLDER GATE, `validate_pr`) only knows the expensive cure — a fresh-sha silent update + full
CI re-dispatch — and never tries to conclude the placeholder in place, even though the head carries

pinned context.

reset cap (gh-852 AC2) eventually parks it entirely.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

**Machine author is a deployment knob, never a rule field:** the agents
repo carries no bot login. Every machine-keyed guard (the `notMachine`
filter in `review-external-once`, the `pr_approved` arming gate, the
rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews, the sticky-park RESET) resolves
through one helper — `js/common/machineAuthor.js` →
`resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config)`. The knob is a **comma-separated
LIST of logins** since gh-728 (owner directive 2026-10-05:
`'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` — the CI bot authors its own PRs,
live fa PR #1249): `resolveMachineAuthor` returns the raw string,
`machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties), and the
predicates (`isMachineAuthored` for PR authors — case-sensitive exact
match per entry; `isMachineLogin` for commit actors — case-insensitive)
match ANY entry. Resolution order:

1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — **the JSON parameter at factory setup**.
   The factory-sm reusable workflow takes a `machine-author` input; it
   lands in the `dmtools run` override as
   `{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"<login>"}}}`. This is the
   global level: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml
   `machine-author:`), valid for every repo the factory runs against.
2. `config.machineAuthor` — **the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob**,

   `module.exports = { machineAuthor: 'my-bot' };`
3. `null` — unconfigured. All guards keyed on it are inert: every green
   PR is reviewable, and a PR-anchored APPROVE never arms `pr_approved`
